Confirm the new site redacts any user or model text before updating these counts. bm_telemetry.py fell 23 to 15 on 2026-07-26: eight raw open-and-write pairs in the ledger maintenance paths were replaced by the audited atomic_write primitive, which also closes the audit finding about rewrites landing with default permissions. bm_autosave.py rose 5 to 9 on 2026-07-27 when the snapshot-event record and the per-worktree lock landed (audit findings 1 and 13). Reviewed by the orchestrator site by site, not accepted on the agent's count: the lock is os.open with O_CREAT|O_EXCL at mode 0600 writing only a pid and a timestamp; one site is an integer counter; the rest funnel through _write_text_atomic, a single primitive that writes at 0600 and os.replace's into place. The event record carries git's own error text rather than user or model text, and lands owner-only inside the directory the new git-containment check protects. bm_fence_hook.py entered the inventory on 2026-07-27, and it entered because the gate CAUGHT it rather than because anyone remembered: a new file wrote secrets and the suite refused to pass until it was reviewed. Five sites by this scanner's count, which counts LINES rather than logical writes. Two are the output funnel (stdout for the hook decision, stderr for the fail-open reason). The other three are one single write: the session token file, opened O_CREAT|O_EXCL at mode 0600 inside a 0700 directory so two sessions cannot race for the same name and no other user can read it. The token is 32 random bytes and carries no user or model text. Worth recording that the orchestrator first counted three and was wrong; the number here is the one the gate actually measures, after looking at every line it flags. bm_learn.py entered the inventory on 2026-07-29 with the correction-learning CLI, and the gate caught it rather than anyone remembering. Two sites by this scanner's count, and both are the output funnel: sys.stdout.write and sys.stderr.write inside _out and _err. This file opens no file and writes no path; every database mutation goes through bm_store.py, which stays the single writer. It is listed anyway, and that is the point of the inventory rather than an exception to it: stdout IS a redaction boundary here, because this CLI prints founder rule text. The review: every printed field passes through bm_learning.safe_display, which strips control characters (so a newline inside a rule cannot forge a second rule block in the output) and caps length; candidate raw_text, the most sensitive column in the store, is NEVER printed by default and needs an explicit --show-source that prints a warning first. bm_runtimes.py entered the inventory on 2026-07-29 with the cross-runtime adapter generator, and again the gate caught it rather than anyone remembering. Four sites by this scanner's count, reviewed line by line rather than accepted on the agent's word. Two are the output funnel (_out to stdout, _err to stderr). The other two are one logical write, _write_text: a temp file opened for writing beside the target, then os.replace into place, so a reader or a second emit never sees a half-written instruction file. The redaction question has an unusually clean answer here and it is worth stating rather than assuming: this module writes NOTHING that came from a founder, a model, a transcript, or the store. Every byte it emits is rendered from the RUNTIMES registry and CLI_SURFACE, both literals in its own source, plus a project root path and a relative tools path it computes itself. It never opens the database, never reads a transcript, and never touches the ledger. Default permissions rather than 0600 are correct for exactly that reason: these files are generated public documentation that the founder is expected to copy into a repository and commit, and the destination directory is docs/runtimes, which ships. bm_threads.py fell 8 to 7 on 2026-07-29 (LOOP P12): the handover append into the project root STATE.md is deleted, along with the directory lock that serialized it. Handovers are now rows written inside the lifecycle transition in bm_store.py, and bm_store.write_state_view is the ONLY writer of STATE.md left in the project. Two sites by this scanner's count, and both are the output funnel: sys.stdout.write and sys.stderr.write inside _out and _err. The memories it renders are written by agents that read web pages, files and command output, so a stored memory carrying a newline could forge extra MEMORY, WHY NOW or SOURCE lines inside a block the reading agent has every reason to treat as system authored: the sentinel would have become an amplifier for whatever text an agent happened to store. Proved on the real function: a memory whose content carried an embedded newline plus a forged MEMORY line rendered as exactly three lines. A SECOND CANDIDATE FINDING WAS REFUTED RATHER THAN SHIPPED, and it is recorded because the refutation is the useful half: sentinel prose lands in the sqlite file in cleartext, which looked like the bm_ledger.py gap repeating.
